Parse command-line arguments

argitect.Rd

A pure-R command-line argument parser that reimplements the functionality of the Perl module Getopt::Long without any external dependency, and additionally supports positional arguments.

Usage

argitect(
  ...,
  help_head = NULL,
  help_foot = NULL,
  envir = parent.frame(),
  argv_str = NULL,
  explain = FALSE,
  template_control = list(),
  help_style = argitect_options("help_style"),
  help_width = argitect_options("help_width"),
  value_sep = argitect_options("value_sep")
)

Arguments

...

Argument specifications. They can be given as (specification, description) pairs, a two-column matrix, or a single text template. See Details.

help_head

Head of the help message shown by --help.

help_foot

Foot of the help message shown by --help.

envir

Environment where default values are looked up and parsed values are exported. A list is also accepted and coerced to an environment.

argv_str

A string containing command-line arguments. Only for testing purposes.

explain

If TRUE, print an explanation of each argument specification (its format and simple examples) and return without parsing any command-line arguments.

template_control

A list controlling template help rendering, e.g. list(opt_width = 21).

help_style

The style of the help message: "one-column" or "two-column".

help_width

The width of the help message. A vector of one or two numbers; the second number is only used by the two-column style. Defaults to argitect_options("help_width").

value_sep

The separator used to split multiple values inside a single name=value pair for a vector sub-argument. The default "auto" detects the separator among ",", ";", ":", "|" and "/" by picking the one that satisfies the type and count constraints.

Value

Invisibly, a list of the parsed argument objects. Parsed values are also exported to envir as variables named after the first specification name.

Details

Each argument specification is name[|alias...]=spec. The value part spec consists of an optional mode (i integer, f numeric, s character, l logical) and an optional type ($ scalar, # positional, @ vector, % hash), optionally followed by a bracketed range or sub-argument list. The i mode also accepts extended integer notation: 0x/0X hexadecimal, 0b/0B binary, 0/0o/0O octal (e.g. 0123), and decimal.

  • "number=i": a single integer scalar.

  • "name=s": a single character scalar.

  • "length|size=i": an integer scalar with two names.

  • "tag=i@": an integer vector.

  • "tag=i@{2,}": an integer vector with at least two elements.

  • "param=s%": name=value pairs with character values.

  • "input=s#": one positional argument.

  • "files=s#{}": one or more positional arguments.

  • "verbose!": a logical option, negatable with --no-verbose.

If a variable with the first name already exists in envir (and is not a function), it is used as the default value and the option becomes optional. Logical options always default to FALSE.

Examples

e = new.env()
argitect("count=i", "Number of items.", "verbose!", "Print messages.",
    envir = e, argv_str = "--count 3 --verbose")
e$count
#> [1] 3
e$verbose
#> [1] TRUE
